mainTopic: Repeating ברכות on מצוות: סוכה, לולב, תפילין, נר חנוכה, and several מצוות at once
overview: The גמרא quotes a ברייתא that says the ברכה on לולב is repeated all seven days, but the ברכה on סוכה is said only on the first day. This contradicts רבי יוחנן, who said the opposite. The לולב clash is resolved by splitting between the time of the בית המקדש and nowadays. The סוכה clash is a dispute between תנאים, modeled on רבי and the חכמים arguing about blessing on תפילין each time. In practice we follow רבי and bless on סוכה all seven days. Next the גמרא debates whether לולב after the first day gets a ברכה. It proves from חנוכה lights that רב makes a ברכה on a rabbinic מצוה, and it explains how we can say 'וצונו' on such a מצוה. Then it covers the ברכות for a סוכה that was already standing, and whether many מצוות get one ברכה or separate ones. The הלכה follows רבי יהודה, who says each מצוה gets its own ברכה. The עמוד ends by opening an אגדה contrasting humans with ה׳, which continues on the next עמוד.

steps.title: ברכות when making and taking a לולב
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא teaches that one who makes his own לולב says שהחיינו. When he takes it, he blesses על נטילת לולב, and he repeats this blessing all seven days.
steps.simpleTranslation: Someone who makes a לולב for himself says the שהחיינו blessing. When he picks it up to do the מצוה, he says 'Who commanded us about taking the לולב.' Even though he already said it on the first day, he says it again every day for all seven days.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a ברייתא with the rules for blessings on the לולב.
steps.deeperAnalysis: There are two kinds of blessings here. שהחיינו is said when the person prepares his own לולב. The מצוה blessing is said when he actually takes it to fulfill his obligation. The key rule is that the מצוה blessing is repeated each of the seven days.

keyTerms.meaning: The blessing thanking ה׳ for bringing us to this time
For himself, meaning for his own use
Taking the לולב, the מצוה act
To fulfill his obligation with it

phrases.english: One who makes a lulav for himself says:
"Blessed... Who has given us life, sustained us,
phrases.notes: The ellipsis is in the source and stands for the standard opening of the blessing.

phrases.english: and brought us to this time."
When he takes it to fulfill his obligation, he says:
"Blessed... Who sanctified us with His מצוות
and commanded us concerning the taking of the lulav."

phrases.aramaic: וְאַף עַל פִּי שֶׁבֵּירַךְ עָלָיו יוֹם רִאשׁוֹן,
phrases.english: And even though he blessed over it on the first day,
he repeats and blesses all seven days.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens this passage by quoting a ברייתא that will be compared to רבי יוחנן's earlier ruling.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The לולב blessing is repeated every day of the seven days.

steps.title: ברכות when making and entering a סוכה
steps.stepSummary: The same ברייתא continues. One who makes his own סוכה says שהחיינו. On entering he blesses לישב בסוכה, but only on the first day.
steps.simpleTranslation: Someone who builds a סוכה for himself says שהחיינו. When he goes in to sit in it, he says 'Who commanded us to sit in the סוכה.' Once he said this blessing on the first day, he does not say it again.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא now gives the parallel rules for the סוכה. Here the rule is the opposite of the לולב: the blessing is said only on the first day.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The structure matches the לולב case: שהחיינו when making it, and a מצוה blessing when using it. The difference is that the סוכה blessing is not repeated. This is because the seven days of סוכה are treated as one continuous מצוה.

keyTerms.meaning: To sit, or dwell, in the סוכה

steps.whatToRemember: According to the ברייתא, you bless on the לולב every day, but on the סוכה only on the first day.

phrases.english: One who makes a sukkah for himself says:
"Blessed... Who has given us life, sustained us, etc."
When he enters to sit in it, he says:
"Who sanctified us with His מצוות
and commanded us to sit in the sukkah,"
and once he has blessed on the first day,
he no longer blesses again.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the same ברייתא, moving from לולב to סוכה.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The סוכה blessing is said only on the first day.

steps.title: The ברייתא contradicts רבי יוחנן on both לולב and סוכה
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא clashes with רבי יוחנן's ruling about both the לולב and the סוכה.
steps.simpleTranslation: There is a contradiction between one ruling on לולב and the other ruling on לולב. There is also a contradiction between one ruling on סוכה and the other ruling on סוכה.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא points out that this ברייתא contradicts what רבה בר בר חנה quoted from רבי יוחנן just before. רבי יוחנן said: bless on the לולב one day, and on the סוכה seven days.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי יוחנן's ruling is the exact reverse of the ברייתא. He says the לולב blessing is said only on the first day, while the סוכה blessing is said all seven days. So there are two separate contradictions, one for each מצוה.

keyTerms.meaning: It is difficult; there is a contradiction
One ruling on לולב against the other ruling on לולב
One ruling on סוכה against the other ruling on סוכה

steps.confusionAlert: The other side of the contradiction is not written here. It is רבי יוחנן's statement quoted earlier on the דף. Without it, the קשיא seems to come from nowhere.

phrases.english: There is a contradiction between lulav and lulav,
and a contradiction between sukkah and sukkah!

steps.triggerLanguage: קַשְׁיָא לוּלָב אַלּוּלָב, קַשְׁיָא סוּכָּה אַסּוּכָּה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Sets the ברייתא against רבי יוחנן's earlier ruling.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי יוחנן's ruling (via רבה בר בר חנה): לולב one day, סוכה seven days
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The ברייתא rules the exact opposite on both מצוות.

steps.title: The לולב contradiction is resolved by the time of the בית המקדש versus today
steps.stepSummary: The לולב contradiction goes away. The ברייתא speaks of the time when the בית המקדש stood, and רבי יוחנן speaks of nowadays.
steps.simpleTranslation: The contradiction between the two לולב rulings is not a problem. One ruling speaks of the time when the בית המקדש stood. The other speaks of the time when the בית המקדש does not stand.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the לולב part of the question by saying each source speaks about a different time period.
steps.deeperAnalysis: When the בית המקדש stood, the לולב was taken all seven days there as a תורה obligation, so each day needed its own blessing. This is the case of the ברייתא. Nowadays, only the first day is from the תורה, so רבי יוחנן rules that the blessing is said only on the first day.

keyTerms.meaning: Here... there; this case versus that case

phrases.english: Granted, lulav against lulav is not difficult:
here, when the Temple is standing,

phrases.aramaic: כָּאן בִּזְמַן שֶׁאֵין בֵּית הַמִּקְדָּשׁ קַיָּים.
phrases.english: there, when the Temple is not standing.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Resolves the first half of the קשיא.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Splitting the cases (אוקימתא by time period)
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The two לולב rulings speak about the same situation and disagree.
steps.terutzMaskana: The ברייתא speaks of the time of the בית המקדש, and רבי יוחנן speaks of nowadays.

steps.title: The סוכה contradiction still stands
steps.stepSummary: The time-period answer does not work for סוכה, so that contradiction remains.
steps.simpleTranslation: But the contradiction between the two סוכה rulings is still a problem!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא says the second half of the question is still open. This sets up the next answer.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The מצוה of סוכה is the same whether or not the בית המקדש stands, so the time-period answer cannot explain it. The question remains: are the seven days one long מצוה (the ברייתא) or seven separate ones (רבי יוחנן)?

phrases.english: But sukkah against sukkah is difficult!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Narrows the original קשיא to the part still unanswered.
steps.kashyaTarget: The conflict between the ברייתא and רבי יוחנן on the סוכה blessing
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The time-period answer does not apply to סוכה, so the contradiction remains.

steps.title: The סוכה question is a dispute between תנאים, modeled on תפילין
steps.stepSummary: The two סוכה rulings follow two sides of a dispute between תנאים. The dispute is seen in a ברייתא on תפילין between רבי and the חכמים.
steps.simpleTranslation: It is a dispute between תנאים. As a ברייתא teaches: with תפילין, every time a person puts them on he blesses on them; these are the words of רבי. The חכמים say he blesses only in the morning.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that the two סוכה rulings simply follow two sides of an older argument. It brings a ברייתא about תפילין to show that argument.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי holds that each new act of putting on תפילין is a new מצוה needing a new blessing. רבי יוחנן's 'bless on סוכה every day' fits this view. The חכמים hold that one morning blessing covers the whole day's wearing, like the ברייתא's view that one blessing on the first day covers all seven days of סוכה.

keyTerms.meaning: It is a dispute between תנאים
As it was taught in a ברייתא

steps.whatToRemember: The ברייתא and רבי יוחנן do not contradict on their own terms. They follow the חכמים and רבי respectively: does one blessing cover a continuing מצוה, or does each new act need its own blessing?
steps.confusionAlert: The ברייתא about תפילין never mentions סוכה. The גמרא is using it as a parallel case: the same principle is at stake in both.

phrases.english: It is a dispute of Tannaim.
As it was taught: tefillin,
every time one puts them on, he blesses over them,
these are the words of Rabbi.
And the Sages say:
he blesses only in the morning.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the remaining סוכה contradiction by tying each ruling to one side of a dispute between תנאים.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Both rulings should agree, so their disagreement is a contradiction.
steps.terutzMaskana: רבי יוחנן follows רבי (each act needs a new blessing). The ברייתא follows the חכמים (one blessing covers a continuing מצוה).
steps.whyThisMatters: This sets up a basic principle in the laws of blessings. When a מצוה continues over time or is interrupted, does one blessing cover it, or does each new act need a fresh blessing?

steps.title: אביי and רבא disagree on whose view is the הלכה
steps.stepSummary: אביי rules like רבי, and רבא rules like the רבנן, in the תפילין dispute.
steps.simpleTranslation: It was stated: אביי said the הלכה follows רבי, and רבא said the הלכה follows the רבנן.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a later argument between אמוראים about which side of the תפילין dispute is the final halacha.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 6 showed that the two סוכה rulings match the two sides of the רבי versus חכמים dispute about תפילין. Now we learn how that dispute is decided. אביי follows רבי, who holds that each time you put on תפילין again you make a new ברכה. רבא follows the רבנן, who hold that one ברכה in the morning covers the whole day.

keyTerms.meaning: It was stated (introduces a dispute between אמוראים)
The Sages, here the חכמים who disagree with רבי

phrases.english: It was stated: Abaye said: The halacha is like Rabbi;
and Rava said: The halacha is like the Rabbis.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Decides the תנאים dispute that step 6 used to explain the two סוכה rulings.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: אביי: הלכה like רבי (a new ברכה each time). רבא: הלכה like the רבנן (one ברכה for the day).

steps.title: רבא's own practice with תפילין
steps.stepSummary: רב מרי saw רבא make a new ברכה each time he put his תפילין back on after using the bathroom.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב מרי, the son of שמואל's daughter, said: I saw רבא not act according to his own ruling. Instead, he would get up early, go into the bathroom, come out, wash his hands, put on תפילין, and make a ברכה. When he needed to go again, he went into the bathroom, came out, washed his hands, put on תפילין, and made a ברכה again.
steps.whatsHappening: An eyewitness reports what רבא actually did. In practice he made a ברכה every time he put his תפילין back on.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבא ruled like the רבנן, who say one ברכה is enough for the day. Yet in practice he took his תפילין off for the bathroom and then made a fresh ברכה when he put them back on. That is the practice of רבי. The report shows that real practice leaned toward רבי's view.

keyTerms.meaning: The bathroom (תפילין are removed before entering)

steps.confusionAlert: Do not think רבא simply changed his mind in words. His stated ruling stayed like the רבנן. What is reported here is his personal practice, which followed רבי.

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רַב מָרִי בְּרַהּ דְּבַת שְׁמוּאֵל:
phrases.english: Rav Mari, son of the daughter of Shmuel, said:
I saw Rava
that he did not act according to his own ruling;

phrases.aramaic: אֶלָּא מַקְדֵּים וְקָאֵי וְעָיֵיל בֵּית הַכִּסֵּא,
phrases.english: rather, he rises early and enters the bathroom,
and comes out and washes his hands,
and puts on tefillin and makes a blessing.
And when he needs to go another time,
he enters the bathroom,
and comes out and washes his hands,
and puts on tefillin and makes a blessing.

steps.triggerLanguage: חֲזֵינָא לֵיהּ לְרָבָא דְּלָא עָבֵיד כִּשְׁמַעְתֵּיהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Tests רבא's ruling from step 7 against his own conduct.
steps.raayaObject: That practice follows רבי (a new ברכה each time the מצוה is resumed).
steps.raayaSupportSource: רב מרי's eyewitness report of רבא's daily conduct.

steps.title: We follow רבי and bless on סוכה all seven days
steps.stepSummary: The practical conclusion is that we follow רבי and make the סוכה ברכה all seven days.
steps.simpleTranslation: And we, too, act like רבי, and we make the ברכה all seven days.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא states the bottom line. For סוכה we follow רבי and say לישב בסוכה on every day of the חג, not only the first.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 6 already removed the contradiction from step 5 by tying the two סוכה rulings to the רבי and חכמים dispute. This step decides which side we follow. Because practice follows רבי, the סוכה ruling that matches רבי wins. That is רבי יוחנן's view: a ברכה every day.

keyTerms.meaning: All seven days of the חג

steps.whatToRemember: The הלכה follows רבי. A מצוה that is stopped and started again gets a new ברכה. So the ברכה לישב בסוכה is said on all seven days.
steps.whyThisMatters: This is the source for the practice of saying לישב בסוכה every day of סוכות.

phrases.english: And we, too, act like Rabbi,
and we make the blessing all seven days.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Draws the practical ruling from רבא's conduct.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: הלכה like רבי: a ברכה on סוכה every day of the seven days.

steps.title: More reports of a ברכה on תפילין each time
steps.stepSummary: רב פפי made a ברכה whenever he put on תפילין, and the scholars of רב אשי's school made one whenever they handled them.
steps.simpleTranslation: מר זוטרא said: I saw רב פפי make a ברכה every time he put on תפילין. The scholars of רב אשי's school made a ברכה every time they handled them.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא adds two more reports of practice. Both show people making repeated ברכות on תפילין, the way רבי holds.
steps.deeperAnalysis: These reports strengthen the conclusion that practice follows רבי. The scholars of רב אשי's school went even further. They made a ברכה each time they touched or adjusted the תפילין, not only when putting them on again.

keyTerms.meaning: The scholars of רב אשי's study hall

phrases.english: Mar Zutra said:
I saw Rav Pappi,
that whenever he put on tefillin he made a blessing.
The Sages of the school of Rav Ashi,
whenever they touched them, made a blessing.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר מָר זוּטְרָא: חֲזֵינָא לֵיהּ לְרַב פַּפֵּי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds supporting reports of practice in line with רבי.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Repeated ברכות on תפילין were the practice of רב פפי and of רב אשי's school.

steps.title: Three views on לולב after the first day
steps.stepSummary: שמואל: a ברכה on לולב all seven days. רבי יהושע בן לוי: a מצוה from the תורה on day one, מצות זקנים afterward. רבי יצחק: every day is מצות זקנים.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב יהודה said in the name of שמואל: the מצוה of לולב is all seven days. רבי יהושע בן לוי said: on the first day it is the מצוה of לולב, and from then on it is a מצות זקנים. רבי יצחק said: every day is a מצות זקנים.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא opens a new topic about לולב. It lists three opinions on the status of the מצוה and its ברכה during the חג.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Outside the בית המקדש, the תורה requires לולב only on the first day. The other days are a rabbinic enactment called מצות זקנים. שמואל holds the ברכה is made all seven days. רבי יהושע בן לוי treats the later days as only מצות זקנים, which Sefaria reads as needing no ברכה. רבי יצחק's wording seems to cover even day one, which sets up the next question.

keyTerms.meaning: A מצוה of the Elders, a rabbinic enactment remembering the מקדש
The palm branch taken with the other species on סוכות

phrases.english: Rav Yehuda said in the name of Shmuel:
The מצוה of lulav is all seven days.
And Rabbi Yehoshua ben Levi said:
The first day is the מצוה of lulav;
from then on it is a מצוה of the Elders.
And Rabbi Yitzchak said:
Every day is a מצוה of the Elders.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב יְהוּדָה אָמַר שְׁמוּאֵל: מִצְוַת לוּלָב כׇּל שִׁבְעָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new topic: the ברכה on לולב during the later days.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A three-way dispute over whether days two through seven of לולב get a ברכה.

steps.title: Can the first day be only rabbinic?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks how רבי יצחק can call even day one a מצות זקנים, when day one is a מצוה from the תורה.
steps.simpleTranslation: Even the first day? But we hold that the first day is from the תורה!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges רבי יצחק's wording, because it seems to make day one rabbinic too.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Everyone agrees that the תורה commands לולב on the first day everywhere. So 'every day' cannot literally include day one. The wording of רבי יצחק's statement must be wrong.

keyTerms.meaning: We hold / it is established for us

phrases.english: And even the first day?!
But we hold
that the first day is by Torah law!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks רבי יצחק's statement from step 11.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Day one is a מצוה from the תורה, so it cannot be called only a מצות זקנים.

steps.title: Correct the wording to exclude the first day
steps.stepSummary: Read רבי יצחק's statement as 'every day except the first day.'
steps.simpleTranslation: Say instead: except for the first day.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא fixes the problem by correcting the text of רבי יצחק's statement.
steps.deeperAnalysis: With the correction, רבי יצחק means that days two through seven are a מצות זקנים. Day one stays a מצוה from the תורה, so the clash with the law of the תורה disappears.

keyTerms.meaning: Say / read it as (a correction of the text)

phrases.english: Say: except for the first day.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge in step 12.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Correcting the text of the statement
steps.terutzHavaAmina: רבי יצחק calls every day, including day one, rabbinic.
steps.terutzMaskana: רבי יצחק means only days two through seven.

steps.title: Then רבי יצחק says the same as רבי יהושע בן לוי
steps.stepSummary: After the correction, רבי יצחק says exactly what רבי יהושע בן לוי says, so why is he quoted as a separate view?
steps.simpleTranslation: If so, that is the same as רבי יהושע בן לוי!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא points out that the correction creates a new problem: the two opinions are now identical.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 11 presented רבי יצחק as a separate opinion. After the fix in step 13, his view is the same as רבי יהושע בן לוי's. A third opinion that adds nothing new does not make sense.

phrases.aramaic: אִי הָכִי — הַיְינוּ דְּרַבִּי יְהוֹשֻׁעַ בֶּן לֵוִי!
phrases.english: If so, that is the same as Rabbi Yehoshua ben Levi!

steps.triggerLanguage: אִי הָכִי הַיְינוּ דְּרַבִּי יְהוֹשֻׁעַ בֶּן לֵוִי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the correction made in step 13.
steps.kashyaTarget: The presentation of רבי יצחק as a separate opinion.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: After the correction there is no difference between the two views.

steps.title: רבי יצחק agrees with רבי יהושע בן לוי
steps.stepSummary: Change the introduction to 'and likewise said רבי יצחק.' He is agreeing, not arguing.
steps.simpleTranslation: Say: and so too said רבי יצחק.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא corrects the introduction so that רבי יצחק is presented as supporting רבי יהושע בן לוי.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The text should not read as if רבי יצחק is arguing. It should say 'וכן אמר', meaning he holds the same view. That leaves two opinions: שמואל, and רבי יהושע בן לוי together with רבי יצחק.

phrases.english: Say: And likewise said Rabbi Yitzchak.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Resolves the challenge in step 14.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Correcting the text of the introduction
steps.terutzHavaAmina: רבי יצחק is a third, separate view.
steps.terutzMaskana: רבי יצחק agrees with רבי יהושע בן לוי.

steps.title: רב also holds לולב gets a ברכה all seven days
steps.stepSummary: רב agrees with שמואל, since he requires a ברכה on lighting נר חנוכה, which is a rabbinic מצוה.
steps.simpleTranslation: And רב also holds that the מצוה of לולב is all seven days. For רבי חייא בר אשי said in the name of רב: one who lights a נר חנוכה must make a ברכה.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא adds רב to שמואל's side. It proves this from רב's ruling about חנוכה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: נר חנוכה is only a rabbinic מצוה, yet רב requires a ברכה on it. So in רב's view a rabbinic מצוה gets a ברכה. The same logic applies to לולב on days two through seven, even though those days are only a מצות זקנים.
steps.whyThisMatters: This sets up a key principle: a rabbinic מצוה also gets a ברכה. That is why we make a ברכה on לולב every day and on חנוכה lights.

phrases.english: And Rav, too, holds:
All seven days are the מצוה of lulav.

phrases.aramaic: דְּאָמַר רַבִּי חִיָּיא בַּר אָשֵׁי אָמַר רַב:
phrases.english: As Rabbi Chiyya bar Ashi said in the name of Rav:

phrases.aramaic: הַמַּדְלִיק נֵר שֶׁל חֲנוּכָּה — צָרִיךְ לְבָרֵךְ.
phrases.english: One who lights a Hanukkah light must make a blessing.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאַף רַב סָבַר: כׇּל שִׁבְעָה מִצְוַת לוּלָב
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds רב in support of שמואל's view from step 11.
steps.raayaObject: רב holds that a ברכה is made on לולב all seven days.
steps.raayaSupportSource: רב's ruling that lighting נר חנוכה, a rabbinic מצוה, requires a ברכה.

steps.title: One who sees a נר חנוכה must bless
steps.stepSummary: רבי ירמיה rules that even someone who only sees a נר חנוכה must make a ברכה.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי ירמיה said: one who sees a נר חנוכה must make a ברכה.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a related ruling about חנוכה. This one applies to a person who sees the lights but does not light them.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב spoke about the person lighting. רבי ירמיה adds that a person who sees the lights also makes a ברכה, to praise the miracle. This sets up the question of which ברכות each person says.

phrases.english: Rabbi Yirmeya said:

phrases.aramaic: הָרוֹאֶה נֵר שֶׁל חֲנוּכָּה — צָרִיךְ לְבָרֵךְ.
phrases.english: One who sees a Hanukkah light must make a blessing.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַבִּי יִרְמְיָה אָמַר: הָרוֹאֶה נֵר שֶׁל חֲנוּכָּה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Extends the חנוכה ברכה rule from the one who lights to the one who sees.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Seeing נר חנוכה requires a ברכה.

steps.title: Which blessings are said?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks which ברכות the one who lights and the one who sees should say.
steps.simpleTranslation: What ברכה does he say?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks a simple clarifying question, setting up the detailed answer that comes next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: We now know that both the one who lights and the one who sees make a ברכה. We do not yet know which ברכות, or how many, each person says.

phrases.english: What blessing does he say?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for details about the rulings in steps 16 and 17.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The exact ברכות for the one who lights and the one who sees.

steps.title: Number of חנוכה ברכות for the lighter and the viewer
steps.stepSummary: Day one: the lighter says three ברכות and the viewer says two. After that: the lighter says two and the viewer says one.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב יהודה said: on the first day, the one who lights says three ברכות and the one who sees says two. From then on, the one who lights says two and the one who sees says one.
steps.whatsHappening: רב יהודה answers the question. He gives the number of ברכות for each person, on the first night and on the later nights.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The three ברכות are להדליק נר חנוכה, שעשה נסים, and שהחיינו. The viewer does not light, so he skips להדליק and says only the other two. After the first night שהחיינו drops out, which leaves two for the lighter and one (שעשה נסים) for the viewer.
steps.whatToRemember: חנוכה: on night one the lighter says 3 ברכות and the viewer says 2. On later nights the lighter says 2 and the viewer says 1. שהחיינו is said only on the first night.
steps.confusionAlert: שהחיינו is said only the first time. That is why each count goes down by one after the first night.

phrases.english: Rav Yehuda said:
On the first day, the one who lights says three blessings;
the one who sees says two.
From then on, the one who lights says two,
and the one who sees says one.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב יְהוּדָה: יוֹם רִאשׁוֹן, הַמַּדְלִיק מְבָרֵךְ שָׁלֹשׁ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question in step 18.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: Lighter: 3 ברכות on night one, then 2. Viewer: 2 on night one, then 1.

steps.title: The wording of the ברכה on נר חנוכה
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks what the main ברכה is and answers: 'אשר קדשנו במצותיו וצונו להדליק נר של חנוכה.'
steps.simpleTranslation: And what ברכה does he say? 'Blessed... Who made us holy with His מצוות and commanded us to light the חנוכה light.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא spells out the exact wording of the ברכה over lighting נר חנוכה, which was one of the ברכות counted in the last step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The words 'וצונו' ('and He commanded us') are the important part. נר חנוכה is a rabbinic מצוה, so it sounds strange to say that ה׳ commanded it. This wording sets up the question in the next step.

keyTerms.meaning: Who made us holy with His מצוות

phrases.english: And what blessing does he say?
"Blessed... Who made us holy with His מצוות
and commanded us to light the Chanukah light."

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Spells out the wording of one of the ברכות listed in step 19.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The exact wording of the ברכה on נר חנוכה.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: 'אשר קדשנו במצותיו וצונו להדליק נר של חנוכה.'

steps.title: Where did ה׳ command us to light?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks how we can say 'and He commanded us' when חנוכה is not in the תורה.
steps.simpleTranslation: And where did He command us?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the wording of the ברכה. חנוכה is not in the תורה, so where did ה׳ ever command us to light?
steps.deeperAnalysis: The question is not about whether to light. It is about whether the ברכה's words are true. If the words 'וצונו' are false, then perhaps we cannot make a ברכה on a rabbinic מצוה at all.
steps.confusionAlert: Nobody is doubting that we light. The only question is how we can honestly say 'ה׳ commanded us' about a מצוה that the חכמים made.

phrases.english: And where did He command us?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the word 'וצונו' in the ברכה quoted in step 20.
steps.kashyaTarget: The phrase 'וצונו' in the ברכה over a rabbinic מצוה.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: חנוכה does not appear in the תורה, so saying that ה׳ commanded it seems false.

steps.title: The source is 'לא תסור'
steps.stepSummary: The תורה's command not to stray from what the חכמים say makes following them a מצוה from ה׳.
steps.simpleTranslation: From 'Do not turn aside' (from what the חכמים tell you).
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that ה׳ did command it, in a general way. The פסוק 'לא תסור' tells us to obey the חכמים.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Every rabbinic מצוה is connected to a תורה command to listen to the חכמים. So when we light נר חנוכה, we are doing what ה׳ told us, and 'וצונו' is true.

keyTerms.meaning: 'Do not turn aside' (דברים יז:יא), the command to follow the חכמים

steps.whyThisMatters: This idea explains why we say 'וצונו' on every rabbinic מצוה with a ברכה, such as נטילת ידים, הלל, and מגילה.

phrases.english: From "Do not turn aside."
phrases.notes: דברים יז:יא — do not stray from what the judges/Sages tell you.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the קשיא of step 21.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Source identification: a general תורה command covers rabbinic מצוות.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Since חנוכה is not written in the תורה, 'וצונו' would be untrue.
steps.terutzMaskana: ה׳ commanded us to obey the חכמים, so following their מצוות is following His command.

steps.title: רב נחמן בר יצחק: the source is 'שאל אביך'
steps.stepSummary: רב נחמן בר יצחק gives a different פסוק as the source: 'Ask your father and he will tell you.'
steps.simpleTranslation: רב נחמן בר יצחק said: 'Ask your father and he will tell you.'
steps.whatsHappening: רב נחמן בר יצחק offers a second answer to the same question, using a different פסוק.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The idea stays the same: the תורה tells us to listen to our elders and חכמים. Only the source פסוק changes, to 'שאל אביך ויגדך, זקניך ויאמרו לך' (דברים לב:ז).

keyTerms.meaning: 'Ask your father and he will tell you' (דברים לב:ז)
An אמורא who gives a different source here

phrases.english: And Rav Nachman bar Yitzchak said:
"Ask your father and he will tell you."
phrases.notes: דברים לב:ז — continues 'your elders, and they will say to you.'

steps.relationToPreviousStep: A second answer to the same question, using a different פסוק.
steps.terutzMaskana: The command to obey the elders comes from 'שאל אביך ויגדך.'

steps.title: After the first night, שהחיינו is dropped
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks which ברכה is dropped after night one and answers that it is זמן (שהחיינו).
steps.simpleTranslation: Which ברכה does he leave out? The ברכה of 'time' (שהחיינו).
steps.whatsHappening: Step 19 said the lighter goes from three ברכות to two after the first night. The גמרא now explains which ברכה drops out: שהחיינו.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The three ברכות on night one are להדליק, שעשה נסים, and שהחיינו. On later nights we drop שהחיינו, the ברכה on reaching this time of year.

phrases.english: (What does he leave out? — The blessing of time.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Clarifies the count in step 19 (three on night one, then two).
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Which ברכה is dropped on the later nights.

steps.title: Why not drop the miracle ברכה instead?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא suggests that perhaps שעשה נסים should be the ברכה that is dropped.
steps.simpleTranslation: Say instead that he leaves out the ברכה of the miracle?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the answer. Maybe the ברכה on the miracle should be the one that drops after the first night.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The miracle could be seen as something we thank ה׳ for once, like שהחיינו. So the גמרא asks why the choice falls on זמן and not נס.

keyTerms.meaning: Miracle: the ברכה of שעשה נסים

phrases.english: Say that he leaves out the blessing of the miracle?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the answer in step 24.
steps.kashyaTarget: The claim that זמן is the ברכה that is dropped.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: שעשה נסים could just as easily be a one-time ברכה.

steps.title: The miracle happened every day
steps.stepSummary: The miracle continued on all eight days, so its ברכה stays. שהחיינו applies only the first time.
steps.simpleTranslation: The miracle was there every day.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that the miracle lasted all eight days, so we thank ה׳ for it each night.
steps.deeperAnalysis: שהחיינו is about reaching a new season, and that happens only once. The miracle of the oil happened anew each day, so its ברכה belongs on every night.

phrases.english: The miracle is there every day.)

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the קשיא of step 25.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Distinction between a one-time event and an ongoing one.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The miracle ברכה might be said only once.
steps.terutzMaskana: The miracle continued daily, so שעשה נסים is said nightly. Only שהחיינו drops.

steps.title: רב explicitly: a ברכה on לולב all seven days
steps.stepSummary: רב נחמן בר יצחק reports that רב said openly that the מצוה of לולב, with its ברכה, applies all seven days.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב נחמן בר יצחק taught it openly: רב said, 'All seven days are the מצוה of לולב.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא returns to the main question about לולב. Earlier we only figured out רב's view from נר חנוכה. Now we hear that רב said it directly.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In step 16, רב's view was an inference: he makes a ברכה on a rabbinic מצוה like חנוכה, so he would make one on לולב after day one. Here רב נחמן בר יצחק says there is no need to infer, because רב stated outright that לולב is a מצוה, with a ברכה, all seven days.
steps.whatToRemember: According to רב, we make a ברכה on לולב all seven days of סוכות, even though after the first day the מצוה outside the מקדש is only rabbinic.

phrases.aramaic: רַב נַחְמָן בַּר יִצְחָק מַתְנֵי לַהּ בְּהֶדְיָא,
phrases.english: Rav Nachman bar Yitzchak taught it explicitly:
Rav said:
All seven days are the מצוה of lulav.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַב נַחְמָן בַּר יִצְחָק מַתְנֵי לַהּ בְּהֶדְיָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Replaces the inference of step 16 with an explicit statement of רב.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: There is a מצוה of לולב, with a ברכה, on all seven days.

steps.title: Building and entering a סוכה: which ברכות
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא teaches that one who builds a סוכה says שהחיינו, and on entering to sit in it says 'אשר קדשנו... לישב בסוכה.'
steps.simpleTranslation: The חכמים taught: One who builds a סוכה for himself says 'Blessed... שהחיינו.' When he goes in to sit in it, he says 'Blessed... אשר קדשנו (לישב בסוכה).'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא opens a new topic with a ברייתא about the ברכות connected to a סוכה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: There are two separate moments. Building the סוכה is a new and happy event, so it gets שהחיינו. Actually sitting in it is the מצוה itself, so that is when the מצוה ברכה 'לישב בסוכה' is said.

keyTerms.meaning: The ברכה 'Who has kept us alive'

phrases.english: The Rabbis taught:
One who makes a sukkah for himself
says: "Blessed... Who has kept us alive, etc."
When he enters to sit in it,
he says: "Blessed... Who made us holy, etc."
phrases.notes: i.e., '...and commanded us to sit in the סוכה.'

steps.relationToPreviousStep: New topic: from the ברכות of לולב and חנוכה to the ברכות of סוכה.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Building a סוכה earns שהחיינו. Sitting in it earns the ברכה 'לישב בסוכה.'

steps.title: A סוכה that was already standing
steps.stepSummary: If the סוכה was already built, he says שהחיינו when he adds something new to it. If he cannot, he says both ברכות when he first sits in it.
steps.simpleTranslation: If it was already built and standing: if he can add something new to it, he makes the ברכה (שהחיינו). If not, when he goes in to sit in it, he makes two ברכות.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא continues with a different case: a סוכה that was already standing, not freshly built for the מצוה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Since he did not build it, there is no building moment for שהחיינו. If he adds something new for the מצוה, that creates a new moment for שהחיינו. If he adds nothing, he says both 'לישב בסוכה' and שהחיינו together when he first sits in it.

keyTerms.meaning: To add something new to it

phrases.english: If it was already made and standing,

phrases.aramaic: אִם יָכוֹל לְחַדֵּשׁ בָּהּ דָּבָר — מְבָרֵךְ.
phrases.english: if he can add something new to it — he makes the blessing.
If not, when he enters to sit in it —
he makes two blessings.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the same ברייתא with the case of a סוכה that already existed.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: For an already-standing סוכה: say שהחיינו if something new is added. Otherwise, say both ברכות on first sitting.

steps.title: רב כהנא said them all over the קידוש cup
steps.stepSummary: רב אשי saw רב כהנא saying all these ברכות over the cup of קידוש.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב אשי said: I saw רב כהנא, who said all of them over the cup of קידוש.
steps.whatsHappening: רב אשי reports what he saw: רב כהנא said the סוכה ברכות together with קידוש, over the cup of wine.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In practice, רב כהנא did not say שהחיינו while building. He joined לישב בסוכה and שהחיינו to the קידוש on the first night of יום טוב. This is how we generally do it today.
steps.whyThisMatters: This matches our custom: on the first night of סוכות we say לישב בסוכה and שהחיינו as part of קידוש.

phrases.english: Rav Ashi said:
I saw Rav Kahana
saying all of them
over the cup of kiddush.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב אָשֵׁי חֲזֵינָא לֵיהּ לְרַב כָּהֲנָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Shows how the ברייתא's ברכות were done in practice.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: All the סוכה ברכות may be said together over the cup of קידוש.

steps.title: Many מצוות: one combined ברכה
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא says that one with many מצוות before him says a single ברכה: 'וצונו על המצות.'
steps.simpleTranslation: The חכמים taught: If many מצוות were in front of him, he says: 'Blessed... Who made us holy with His מצוות and commanded us about the מצוות.'
steps.whatsHappening: A new ברייתא opens a new question: what to do when someone has several מצוות to do at once. The first opinion says one general ברכה covers them all.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Instead of naming each מצוה, the ברכה ends with the general words 'על המצות.' That way one ברכה covers everything in front of him.

phrases.english: The Rabbis taught:
If there were many מצוות in front of him,
he says: "Blessed... Who made us holy with His מצוות
and commanded us about the מצוות."

steps.triggerLanguage: תָּנוּ רַבָּנַן הָיוּ לְפָנָיו מִצְוֹת הַרְבֵּה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: New ברייתא on a related topic: ברכות for several מצוות at once.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: One general ברכה, 'על המצות,' covers many מצוות.

steps.title: רבי יהודה: a separate ברכה for each
steps.stepSummary: רבי יהודה disagrees and says each מצוה gets its own ברכה.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יהודה says: He makes a ברכה on each one by itself.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יהודה argues on the first opinion. He says you may not lump the מצוות together under one ברכה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: For רבי יהודה, each מצוה deserves its own specific ברכה, naming what is being done. This creates a מחלוקת that the גמרא will now decide.

phrases.english: Rabbi Yehuda says:

phrases.aramaic: מְבָרֵךְ עַל כׇּל אַחַת וְאַחַת בִּפְנֵי עַצְמָהּ.
phrases.english: He makes a blessing on each and every one by itself.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Disagrees with the first opinion in step 31.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Each מצוה gets its own separate ברכה.

steps.title: The הלכה follows רבי יהודה
steps.stepSummary: רבי זירא (or רבי חנינא בר פפא) rules like רבי יהודה.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי זירא said, and some say it was רבי חנינא בר פפא: The הלכה is like רבי יהודה.
steps.whatsHappening: An אמורא decides the מחלוקת: we follow רבי יהודה and make a separate ברכה on each מצוה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: There is doubt about who said this ruling, רבי זירא or רבי חנינא בר פפא. That doubt does not change the ruling itself.

phrases.english: Rabbi Zeira said,
and some say it was Rabbi Chanina bar Pappa:
The halacha is like Rabbi Yehuda.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Decides the מחלוקת of steps 31-32.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: Make a separate ברכה on each מצוה.

steps.title: What is רבי יהודה's reason?
steps.stepSummary: The same אמורא asks what source רבי יהודה relies on.
steps.simpleTranslation: And רבי זירא said, and some say רבי חנינא בר פפא: What is the reason of רבי יהודה?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא sets up the next move by asking for the source behind רבי יהודה's view.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Now that the הלכה follows רבי יהודה, we want to know why he holds this way. The answer will come from a פסוק.

phrases.english: And Rabbi Zeira said,
and some say it was Rabbi Chanina bar Pappa:
What is the reason of Rabbi Yehuda?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Seeks the reasoning behind the ruling in step 33.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The scriptural source for separate ברכות.

steps.title: The פסוק 'ברוך ה' יום יום' and its puzzle
steps.stepSummary: The source is 'ברוך ה' יום יום.' But does that mean we bless ה׳ by day and not at night?
steps.simpleTranslation: As it is written: 'Blessed is ה׳ day by day.' Do we bless Him only by day and not at night?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings the פסוק and points out that, read literally, it makes no sense. That sets up the true meaning in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Read simply, 'יום יום' would limit blessing ה׳ to daytime. That is obviously not true, so the words must carry a different message.

keyTerms.meaning: 'Blessed is ה׳ day by day' (תהלים סח:כ)
Is it really so that...? (a rhetorical challenge)

phrases.english: As it is written: "Blessed is ה׳ day by day."
Do we really bless Him by day
and at night not bless Him?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Begins the answer to step 34 by citing a פסוק.
steps.raayaObject: רבי יהודה's view that each מצוה gets its own ברכה.

steps.title: Give each thing its own fitting ברכה
steps.stepSummary: The פסוק means: give ה׳ the ברכה that fits each day. Likewise, give each מצוה its own fitting ברכה.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, it comes to teach you: each and every day, give Him the ברכות that fit that day. Here too, for each and every thing, give Him the ברכות that fit it.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains the real meaning of the פסוק and applies it to רבי יהודה's rule.
steps.deeperAnalysis: 'יום יום' means each day gets its own matching praise, such as שבת, יום טוב, or a weekday. In the same way, each מצוה gets its own matching ברכה, and you should not lump them together.

keyTerms.meaning: Rather, it comes to teach you
ברכות that fit it, matching ברכות

steps.whatToRemember: The הלכה follows רבי יהודה: each מצוה gets its own specific ברכה, because 'ברוך ה' יום יום' teaches that each thing should be blessed in its own fitting way.

phrases.english: Rather, it comes to tell you:

phrases.aramaic: בְּכׇל יוֹם וְיוֹם תֵּן לוֹ מֵעֵין בִּרְכוֹתָיו,
phrases.english: each and every day, give Him the blessings that fit it;
here too —

phrases.aramaic: בְּכׇל דָּבָר וְדָבָר תֵּן לוֹ מֵעֵין בִּרְכוֹתָיו.
phrases.english: for each and every thing, give Him the blessings that fit it.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Resolves the puzzle of step 35 and applies it as רבי יהודה's source.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The פסוק teaches that each thing gets its own fitting ברכה.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: Separate, specific ברכות for each מצוה, following רבי יהודה.

steps.title: Human nature is unlike the way of ה׳: the empty vessel
steps.stepSummary: The same אמורא who ruled like רבי יהודה now brings an אגדה. He contrasts the way of humans, בשר ודם, with the way of הקדוש ברוך הוא. He begins with how a human vessel works: an empty vessel can take things in.
steps.simpleTranslation: And רבי זירא said, and some say it was רבי חנינא בר פפא: Come and see that the way of humans is not like the way of הקדוש ברוך הוא. The way of humans is that an empty vessel [can hold things, as the next passage explains].
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is moving from the הלכה about ברכות to an אגדה taught by the same rabbis. This line sets up a contrast between humans and ה׳ and starts describing the human side.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The only reason this teaching appears here is that it comes from the same author as the previous ruling. The structure is a two-part comparison. First comes the human rule, which begins with 'an empty vessel'. Then, on the next amud, comes ה׳'s opposite rule. In the human world only an empty container has room to take something in, and the גמרא is setting up a reversal of that idea.

keyTerms.meaning: 'And some say'. It gives a second opinion about who said the teaching.
'Come and see'. It opens a teaching that invites you to notice something striking.
Here it means a way of acting, a nature or pattern. It does not mean a measurement.

steps.confusionAlert: This is not a new הלכה about ברכות. It is a separate אגדה. The גמרא includes it only because the same rabbi said it. The sentence is also unfinished here: 'an empty vessel' still needs its ending, which says that it holds things, and the contrast with ה׳ comes next.

phrases.english: And Rabbi Zeira said
and some say it was Rabbi Chanina bar Pappa:
phrases.notes: This is the same pair of names as in the previous ruling, which is why this teaching is placed here.

phrases.aramaic: בֹּא וּרְאֵה שֶׁלֹּא כְּמִדַּת הַקָּדוֹשׁ בָּרוּךְ הוּא
phrases.english: Come and see that unlike the way of the Holy One, Blessed be He,
is the way of flesh and blood (humans).
phrases.notes: Human nature and ה׳'s way work differently.

phrases.english: The way of flesh and blood: an empty vessel
phrases.notes: The sentence continues on the next amud: an empty vessel holds things, and a full one does not.

steps.alternativePossibleLabel: מסקנא (unlikely; this opens a new teaching)
steps.triggerLanguage: בֹּא וּרְאֵה שֶׁלֹּא כְּמִדַּת הַקָּדוֹשׁ בָּרוּךְ הוּא מִדַּת בָּשָׂר וְדָם
steps.relationToPreviousStep: This is linked by author only. The same אמורא who ruled like רבי יהודה in Step 33 now gives an unrelated אגדה.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The way of humans is not like the way of הקדוש ברוך הוא. For humans, an empty vessel is what can take things in. The contrast with ה׳'s opposite way follows on the next amud.
